title: OneDrive: improved Copilot file skills in OneDrive on the web
summary: Hold: the rollout checklist assures users that generated outputs follow destination permissions and labels without documentation establishing that behaviour for these skills. Microsoft describes label inheritance from source content where supported, not a blanket destination-label rule. The roadmap facts and the four published control paths and commands check out.

claims.claim: Licence assignment is reached at Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. 2. Select a product. 3. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: The printed Set-MgUserLicense call assigns the selected SKU to the identified user using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is reached at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. 2. Select the site you want to configure. 3. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site ... Use PowerShell ... Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions and references only content the user can access.
claims.quote: Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions. ... Copilot only summarizes or references content that the user is already authorized to access.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Copilot can surface already overshared content to people who have access.
claims.quote: If content is already overshared, Copilot can surface it to anyone who has access.

claims.claim: Both VIEW and EXTRACT usage rights are necessary for Copilot to summarise or return encrypted content.
claims.quote: When content is encrypted, whether by a sensitivity label or by Azure Rights Management without a label, the user must have both the VIEW and EXTRACT usage rights for Copilot to summarize or return the content.

claims.claim: With VIEW but not EXTRACT, Copilot can return a link instead of summarising the content.
claims.quote: If the user has VIEW but not EXTRACT, Copilot doesn't summarize the content, but it can return a link so the user can open it outside Copilot.

claims.claim: Copilot-generated content inherits the highest-priority source label where inheritance is supported.
claims.quote: When Copilot creates new content from labeled items, the label with the highest priority is applied to the new content, where label inheritance is supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A Microsoft Purview DLP policy for Copilot can prevent summarisation of labelled files and emails.
claims.quote: A DLP policy for Copilot can keep Copilot from summarizing labeled files and emails. Copilot can still return a link so the user can open the item outside Copilot.

claims.claim: Saved or shared Copilot outputs follow the labels that apply where they are saved.

Remove those checklist items to satisfy the table-consistency rule without adding unverified rows; retain the supported descriptions in Risk assessment.
